record.paper_title: Higher Rank Brill-Noether Theory and Coherent Systems: Open Questions
record.original_question: Do there exist smooth curves C with classical Clifford index Cliff_1(C)=3 but rank-3 Clifford index Cliff_3(C)=8/3?

evidence.quote: Question 3.6. Do there exist curves with Cliff1(C) = 3 and Cliff3(C) = 8/3?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $C$ be a smooth irreducible complex projective curve of genus $g\ge 2$. For a vector bundle $E$ on $C$ of rank $n$ and degree $d$, define the Clifford index of $E$ by
$$\gamma(E)=\mu(E)-\frac{2}{n}\,h^0(E)+2,\qquad \mu(E)=d/n,$$
and define the rank-$n$ Clifford index of $C$ by
$$\mathrm{Cliff}_n(C)=\min\bigl\{\gamma(E):E\text{ is a semistable bundle on }C\text{ of rank }n\text{ with }h^0(E)\ge 2n\text{ and }\mu(E)\le g-1\bigr\}.$$
In particular $\mathrm{Cliff}_1(C)$ is the classical Clifford index of $C$.

Do there exist smooth irreducible complex projective curves $C$ satisfying
$$\mathrm{Cliff}_1(C)=3\quad\text{and}\quad \mathrm{Cliff}_3(C)=\tfrac{8}{3}?$$
artifact.category_tag: Higher rank Clifford index of curves
artifact.status_search_result: A web search located related works on rank-3 bundles over curves of Clifford index 3 (e.g., Lange–Newstead's work "Bundles of rank 3 on curves of Clifford index 3"), but no source was found that explicitly settles the existence of smooth curves with $\mathrm{Cliff}_1=3$ and $\mathrm{Cliff}_3=8/3$. The current status appears unresolved in the accessible literature.

status_evidence.title: Bundles of rank 3 on curves of Clifford index 3
status_evidence.snippet: Study of rank-3 bundles on curves with classical Clifford index 3 and their higher-rank Clifford indices.
status_evidence.claim: Related work discusses rank-3 bundles on curves of Clifford index 3 but does not settle the specific existence question for Cliff_3=8/3.

status_evidence.title: Clifford Indices for Vector Bundles on Curves
status_evidence.snippet: Definitions and basic results on higher-rank Clifford indices Cliff_n(C).
status_evidence.claim: Provides the framework for Cliff_n(C) used to formulate the question.
